chief_complaint: Post‑myocardial infarction follow‑up and cardiovascular risk management
history_of_present_illness: The patient suffered an acute non‑ST segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) on 2022‑04‑23 and has been managed with secondary‑prevention therapies. Since then, he has persistent essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes‑related kidney involvement manifested as micro‑albuminuria and chronic kidney disease (stage 2). Blood pressure is controlled at 118/85 mmHg, heart rate 90 bpm, and recent A1c is 5.2 % (normal). He continues to take antihypertensives, a beta‑blocker, aspirin, and statins, though the statin regimen appears duplicated and a P2Y12 inhibitor is absent. Socially, he reports limited contact, isolation, and recent intimate‑partner abuse, which may affect adherence. Dental issues (loss of teeth) are also noted. Overall, his clinical course reflects ongoing cardiovascular and renal risk with psychosocial stressors.

Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (recent NSTEMI, hypertension, dyslipidemia), renal (CKD stage 2, diabetic nephropathy), metabolic (type 2 diabetes), and psychosocial (isolation, intimate‑partner abuse). Polypharmacy risk is moderate.
